verdict.rationale: Docs explicitly describe executing Python and JavaScript with rich outputs (charts, tables, formatted data), stateful contexts preserving variables/imports across executions, and automatic return of last expression (e.g., pandas DataFrame sum), plus general shell exec via sandbox.exec(). This covers multi-language execution and rich result output as described. Missing for 10: independent hands-on verification of the rich-output rendering (e.g., actual chart/image output) and confirmation of additional language runtimes beyond Python/JS.
